### `reject-promotion`

<p class="tool-meta">Tier <code>mcp:write</code></p>

Reject a promotion request with a reason. The reason is recorded on the request and in the audit trail — a rejection nobody can explain later is not evidence of a decision.

| Parameter                                     | Type   | Description                                                       |
| --------------------------------------------- | ------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `promotion` <span class="req">required</span> | string | Promotion request uuid.                                           |
| `reason` <span class="req">required</span>    | string | Why it was rejected. Recorded on the request.                     |
| `organization`                                | string | Organisation uuid or slug. Omit to use your default organisation. |

### `run-scheduled-task`

<p class="tool-meta">Tier <code>mcp:write</code> · permission <code>deployments.execute.pipeline</code></p>

Start one scheduled task now, outside its schedule. It runs the command ALREADY DECLARED on the task — no tool on this server takes a command to run. It returns as soon as the unit is started, not when it finishes: read the outcome back with refresh-scheduled-task-status and then get-scheduled-task. A task whose overlap policy is skip and whose previous run is still going will exit 75 and report run_state `skipped`, which is not a failure.

| Parameter                                          | Type   | Description                                                                                          |
| -------------------------------------------------- | ------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `scheduled_task` <span class="req">required</span> | string | Scheduled task uuid, from list-scheduled-tasks. The command that runs is the one stored on the task. |
| `organization`                                     | string | Organisation uuid or slug. Omit to use your default organisation.                                    |

### `set-scheduled-task-enabled`

<p class="tool-meta">Tier <code>mcp:write</code> · permission <code>deployments.update.item</code></p>

Switch one scheduled task on or off. Disabling REMOVES its timer and unit from the node rather than merely disabling them — a switch that lives both in a row and in a file on a machine is a switch with two positions and one label. It takes effect immediately, not on the next deploy. The build preset's own scheduler tick can be switched off here, and doing so stops every queued job and scheduled command in that application, so the response says so plainly. Nothing is deleted: the task keeps its schedule and comes back with its unit when re-enabled.

| Parameter                                          | Type    | Description                                                                                                |
| -------------------------------------------------- | ------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `scheduled_task` <span class="req">required</span> | string  | Scheduled task uuid, from list-scheduled-tasks.                                                            |
| `enabled` <span class="req">required</span>        | boolean | true writes the timer and unit to the node; false removes both. The task record itself is kept either way. |
| `organization`                                     | string  | Organisation uuid or slug. Omit to use your default organisation.                                          |

### `refresh-scheduled-task-status`

<p class="tool-meta">Tier <code>mcp:write</code> · permission <code>deployments.view.list</code></p>

Ask the node how every scheduled task on one application attachment last ran, and record it. This is the only thing that moves run_state — list-scheduled-tasks and get-scheduled-task report what was last recorded, so without this they can be arbitrarily stale. It changes nothing on the machine: it reads the unit's own timestamps and journal. One SSH round trip per task, which is why it is explicit rather than folded into every read. A node that is away leaves each row with what it last knew, and the response names the tasks whose reading did not move.

| Parameter                                    | Type   | Description                                                                                |
| -------------------------------------------- | ------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `workload` <span class="req">required</span> | string | Application attachment uuid, from list-workloads. Every scheduled task on it is refreshed. |
| `organization`                               | string | Organisation uuid or slug. Omit to use your default organisation.                          |

### `check-file-database`

<p class="tool-meta">Tier <code>mcp:write</code> · permission <code>file-databases.update.item</code> · organisation owner or administrator only</p>

Run PRAGMA integrity_check against one recorded SQLite file and store what came back. THREE outcomes, not two: `healthy` (sqlite3 read it and reported it sound), `failed` (sqlite3 read it and objected — a finding about your data) and `undetermined` (the check could not be taken at all: sqlite3 missing, the probe abandoned on timeout, or the file written by a newer SQLite than the node's CLI can read). An undetermined result establishes NOTHING and must never be reported as corruption — `check_is_evidence` is false for it, and `tool_version` is half the answer to why. The file is addressed by its record uuid; this tool takes no path and no command.

| Parameter                                         | Type   | Description                                                                                                  |
| ------------------------------------------------- | ------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `file_database` <span class="req">required</span> | string | File database uuid, from list-file-databases. A path is never accepted here — the record is the only handle. |
| `organization`                                    | string | Organisation uuid or slug. Omit to use your default organisation.                                            |

### `attach-application-cache`

<p class="tool-meta">Tier <code>mcp:write</code> · permission <code>deployments.update.item</code></p>

Point one application at a managed cache instance. Values travel INBOUND ONLY, exactly as set-workload-env does: the response names the environment keys it wrote and never the connection string in them. Re-attaching onto the same instance keeps the recorded key prefix rather than resetting it, because a prefix that moves is a cache that empties. Moving an application onto a DIFFERENT instance leaves everything in the old one — nothing is copied and nothing is flushed — and the response reports that it was repointed. Applies on the next deploy.

| Parameter                                         | Type   | Description                                                                                                                                                                            |
| ------------------------------------------------- | ------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `workload` <span class="req">required</span>      | string | Application attachment uuid, from list-workloads.                                                                                                                                      |
| `managed_cache` <span class="req">required</span> | string | Managed cache uuid, from list-managed-caches.                                                                                                                                          |
| `prefix`                                          | string | Key prefix for this application. Omit on a re-attach to keep the recorded one; omit on a first attach to use the application slug. Two applications sharing a prefix share a keyspace. |
| `organization`                                    | string | Organisation uuid or slug. Omit to use your default organisation.                                                                                                                      |

### `detach-application-cache`

<p class="tool-meta">Tier <code>mcp:write</code> · permission <code>deployments.update.item</code></p>

Stop one application using its managed cache instance. The instance, its data and every other application on it are untouched: what goes is the link, the key prefix and the four environment keys the attach wrote. It is therefore not a destructive tool and takes no retyped confirmation — it is mcp:write, because ending a relationship is not taking infrastructure apart. It IS disruptive: the next deploy runs without the connection string, so an application still caching keeps working until it is redeployed and then falls back to whatever its own config says.

| Parameter                                    | Type   | Description                                                       |
| -------------------------------------------- | ------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `workload` <span class="req">required</span> | string | Application attachment uuid, from list-workloads.                 |
| `organization`                               | string | Organisation uuid or slug. Omit to use your default organisation. |

### `set-backup-policy-destination`

<p class="tool-meta">Tier <code>mcp:write</code> · permission <code>backups.update.item</code> · organisation owner or administrator only</p>

Point backup policies at another destination for their FUTURE runs — the same action as the bulk "Move to destination" on the Backups page. Copies already taken stay where they are and remain restorable; nothing is transferred. The target must be an active destination this organisation can use. A policy whose subject already has a policy at the target with the same prefix is reported under `refused` and left unchanged. Requires a token carrying mcp:write.

| Parameter                                       | Type            | Description                                                             |
| ----------------------------------------------- | --------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `policies` <span class="req">required</span>    | array of string | Backup policy uuids, from list-backup-policies (1-100).                 |
| `destination` <span class="req">required</span> | string          | Target destination uuid, from list-backup-destinations. Must be active. |
| `organization`                                  | string          | Organisation uuid or slug. Omit to use your default organisation.       |

### `create-backup-policy`

<p class="tool-meta">Tier <code>mcp:write</code> · permission <code>backups.create.item</code> · organisation owner or administrator only</p>

Create a backup policy — the same action and the same refusals as the New backup policy form (`CreateBackupPolicyAction`). `subject_kind` is database (a managed database uuid, from list-managed-databases), application (the application uuid, from create-application), storage (a managed bucket uuid) or server (a managed node uuid — captures the node's declared CONFIGURATION, never its files). Refused: another organisation's subject or destination, an inactive destination, a subject no driver can capture, a failing egress preflight (the node cannot reach the destination), an invalid cron, and a second policy for the same subject + destination + prefix. The response names what each run will capture (`captures`) and what it will NOT (`not_covered`) — an application captures its declared volumes, its build preset's shared directories and files when G8Deck runs it natively (storage/ and database/database.sqlite for Laravel, minus regenerable caches, sessions, compiled views and logs), recorded SQLite files, its resolved .env and release manifest — and nothing outside those. The encryption passphrase is generated and stored by G8Deck and is NEVER returned: reveal it on the policy's page in G8Deck (audited, needs backups.download.item) and keep a copy outside G8Deck — it is the only thing that opens a downloaded copy if this control plane is lost. Requires a token carrying mcp:write.

| Parameter                                        | Type    | Description                                                                                                                                            |
| ------------------------------------------------ | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `subject_kind` <span class="req">required</span> | string  | database \| application \| storage \| server. server captures configuration only, never files. One of: `database`, `application`, `storage`, `server`. |
| `subject` <span class="req">required</span>      | string  | Uuid of the subject: a managed database, an application (from create-application), a managed bucket, or a managed node.                                |
| `destination`                                    | string  | Destination uuid, from list-backup-destinations. Omit for the organisation's default (G8Deck Storage when it has none of its own).                     |
| `schedule_cron`                                  | string  | Cron expression in `timezone` (default "0 2 * * *").                                                                                                   |
| `timezone`                                       | string  | IANA timezone the cron is read in (default UTC).                                                                                                       |
| `retention_count`                                | integer | Keep this many verified copies (default from config).                                                                                                  |
| `retention_days`                                 | integer | Keep copies this many days. Omit for no age limit.                                                                                                     |
| `verify_level`                                   | string  | How each copy is verified (default readability). One of: `integrity`, `readability`, `restorability`.                                                  |
| `drill_cron`                                     | string  | Optional cron for a scheduled restore drill.                                                                                                           |
| `destination_prefix`                             | string  | Optional key prefix inside the destination.                                                                                                            |
| `enabled`                                        | boolean | Whether the schedule runs (default true).                                                                                                              |
| `organization`                                   | string  | Organisation uuid or slug. Omit to use your default organisation.                                                                                      |

### `run-backup-policy`

<p class="tool-meta">Tier <code>mcp:write</code> · permission <code>backups.execute.run</code> · organisation owner or administrator only</p>

Run one backup policy now, outside its schedule — the Backups page's "Run now". QUEUED: `RunBackupJob` on the infra redis connection runs `RunBackupAction` (plan, capture, encrypt, upload, verify, prune). The run row is written when a worker claims the job, so there is no run uuid yet — read the outcome with list-backup-runs (`policy`, newest first): a run is only `completed` once its copy verified where it landed. One run per policy at a time: while `in_flight` is set the dispatch collapses into that run. Requires a token carrying mcp:write.

| Parameter                                  | Type   | Description                                                       |
| ------------------------------------------ | ------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `policy` <span class="req">required</span> | string | Backup policy uuid, from list-backup-policies.                    |
| `organization`                             | string | Organisation uuid or slug. Omit to use your default organisation. |

### `set-backup-policy-enabled`

<p class="tool-meta">Tier <code>mcp:write</code> · permission <code>backups.update.item</code> · organisation owner or administrator only</p>

Pause (`enabled: false`) or resume (`enabled: true`) a backup policy's schedule — the Backups page's toggle. Only the schedule stops: every run and every copy is kept and stays restorable, which matters most for a policy whose subject was deleted (it shows `subject.uuid: null` in list-backup-policies) — those copies are the only ones left. Works whether or not the subject still exists. Requires a token carrying mcp:write.

| Parameter                                   | Type    | Description                                                       |
| ------------------------------------------- | ------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `policy` <span class="req">required</span>  | string  | Backup policy uuid, from list-backup-policies.                    |
| `enabled` <span class="req">required</span> | boolean | true resumes the schedule, false pauses it.                       |
| `organization`                              | string  | Organisation uuid or slug. Omit to use your default organisation. |

### `create-application`

<p class="tool-meta">Tier <code>mcp:write</code> · permission <code>deployments.create.item</code></p>

Create an application from a git repository (or with no source yet): name, repository URL — or `repository` (owner/name) picked from list-repositories when the organisation has connected the G8Deck GitHub App —, branch, build preset, runtime version, port, domain and health path. Lands in the named project, or in a new project named after the application when only a team is given. Nothing is placed or deployed — call launch-application next. An SSH repository URL gets its own deploy key, whose PUBLIC half is returned to register on the repository; an HTTPS URL authenticates with the organisation's git credential for that host, if one exists. A repository covered by the GitHub App installation clones with an installation token instead (git_access.method github_app), and an SSH URL's deploy key is then registered on the repository for you.

| Parameter                                | Type    | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| ---------------------------------------- | ------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `name` <span class="req">required</span> | string  | Application name.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `project`                                | string  | Project uuid or slug to add it to. Omit and give team to create a project named after the application.                                                                                                                                                         |
| `team`                                   | string  | Team uuid or slug, when no project is given.                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `source_url`                             | string  | Repository URL: https://…, ssh://… or git@host:owner/repo.git. Omit for an application with no source yet.                                                                                                                                                     |
| `repository`                             | string  | Instead of source_url: owner/name of a repository the organisation's G8Deck GitHub App covers (list-repositories). Cloned over HTTPS with an installation token.                                                                                               |
| `branch`                                 | string  | Branch to build and to track for push-to-deploy. Default main.                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `git_credential`                         | string  | Optional git credential uuid to CHECK against an HTTPS URL (same organisation, same host, holds a token). Credentials are matched by host at clone time; naming one does not bind it.                                                                          |
| `preset`                                 | string  | Build preset: dockerfile (default), static, laravel, node, nextjs, astro, python, django, symfony or go.                                                                                                                                                       |
| `runtime_version`                        | string  | Pin the toolchain version for presets that take one (laravel/symfony → PHP, node/nextjs/astro → Node). Omit to auto-detect at build time from composer.json / package.json / .nvmrc (highest selectable version the repo admits), falling back to the default. |
| `port`                                   | integer | Container/listening port. Defaults to the preset's own port.                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `domain`                                 | string  | Hostname to serve. Refused if another deployment already serves it. More can be added later with add-application-domain.                                                                                                                                       |
| `health_path`                            | string  | HTTP path probed after each deploy. Laravel defaults to /up.                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `organization`                           | string  | Organisation uuid or slug. Omit to use your default organisation.                                                                                                                                                                                              |

### `launch-application`

<p class="tool-meta">Tier <code>mcp:write</code> · permission <code>deployments.create.item</code></p>

Launch an application on a server: creates the deployment in the given environment (production by default), attaches the application to the topology's application layer, wires an optional managed database, and QUEUES provisioning. Returns the deployment uuid — poll get-pipeline-status, or diagnose-deployment if it stops moving. A git repository is probed first: if the clone is refused (deploy key not registered yet), the deployment is created but nothing is queued, and the response says what to fix before calling execute-pipeline. Team server allocation is enforced: a member may launch only on servers allocated to their team.

| Parameter                                       | Type    | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| ----------------------------------------------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `application` <span class="req">required</span> | string  | Application uuid or slug, from create-application.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `server` <span class="req">required</span>      | string  | Infrastructure provider (server) uuid or slug to run it on.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `environment`                                   | string  | Environment type. Default production. The environment row is created if the project has none of this type. One of: `local`, `development`, `staging`, `production`, `dr`, `preview`.                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `blueprint`                                     | string  | Topology blueprint uuid or slug. Omit to compose one from shape.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `shape`                                         | object  | Composed topology when no blueprint is given: {runtime: php\|python\|node, database: mysql\|mariadb\|postgresql\|null, cache: bool, workers: bool, placement: single\|app-data\|edge-app-data}. Omit for a single-server shape with the runtime taken from the preset. Pass database: null when the application uses a managed database server instead. |
| `size`                                          | string  | Deployment size. Default small. One of: `small`, `medium`, `large`, `custom`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `name`                                          | string  | Deployment name. Defaults to "&lt;application&gt; · &lt;Environment&gt;".                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `database_server`                               | string  | Managed database server uuid to give the application its own database on, now. Or attach one later with attach-application-database.                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `deploy`                                        | boolean | Queue provisioning now (default true). False creates the deployment only.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `organization`                                  | string  | Organisation uuid or slug. Omit to use your default organisation.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |

### `attach-application-database`

<p class="tool-meta">Tier <code>mcp:write</code> · permission <code>deployments.update.item</code></p>

Give an application its own database on a managed database server: creates the database, an owner account and the grant (named from the deployment and application slugs), and writes the connection settings into the application's environment. Values travel INBOUND ONLY — the response names the env keys written (DB_HOST, DB_PASSWORD, DATABASE_URL …) and never a value. Re-attaching the same server is a no-op regrant; moving to a different database is refused, because the data would stay behind. The database and account are created by queued jobs and the next deploy waits for them. Applies on the next deploy.

| Parameter                                           | Type   | Description                                                                                         |
| --------------------------------------------------- | ------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `workload` <span class="req">required</span>        | string | Application attachment uuid (the workload uuid launch-application returns, or from list-workloads). |
| `database_server` <span class="req">required</span> | string | Managed database server uuid, from list-database-servers on the platform server.                    |
| `organization`                                      | string | Organisation uuid or slug. Omit to use your default organisation.                                   |

### `add-application-domain`

<p class="tool-meta">Tier <code>mcp:write</code> · permission <code>deployments.update.item</code></p>

Serve an application on a hostname. Sets the domain on one of its ports (the first port by default; give port to pick one, or to declare a port when the application has none) and syncs it into every deployment the application runs in. Refused if another deployment already serves the name. Adding re-queues the pipeline steps that route it, write its DNS record and issue its certificate — call execute-pipeline for each deployment listed, then poll list-application-domains for the DNS and certificate state (a certificate reads pending/issuing until issued, or failed with the reason). Already present: returned unchanged.

| Parameter                                       | Type    | Description                                                                                 |
| ----------------------------------------------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `application` <span class="req">required</span> | string  | Application uuid or slug.                                                                   |
| `domain` <span class="req">required</span>      | string  | Hostname to serve, e.g. app.example.com.                                                    |
| `port`                                          | integer | Which port serves it. Default: the first port. Required when the application declares none. |
| `organization`                                  | string  | Organisation uuid or slug. Omit to use your default organisation.                           |

### `remove-application-domain`

<p class="tool-meta">Tier <code>mcp:write</code> · permission <code>deployments.update.item</code></p>

Stop serving a hostname. Removes it from the application and, in every deployment it runs in, takes down the vhost and certificate and deletes the DNS record if G8Deck created it (a record you created by hand is left alone). The application keeps running on its other names. A domain the application does not serve is reported absent rather than failing.

| Parameter                                       | Type   | Description                                                       |
| ----------------------------------------------- | ------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `application` <span class="req">required</span> | string | Application uuid or slug.                                         |
| `domain` <span class="req">required</span>      | string | Hostname to stop serving.                                         |
| `organization`                                  | string | Organisation uuid or slug. Omit to use your default organisation. |

### `rotate-deploy-webhook-secret`

<p class="tool-meta">Tier <code>mcp:write</code> · permission <code>deployments.update.item</code></p>

Rotate an application's push-to-deploy webhook secret. The old secret stops verifying immediately, so every GitHub delivery is rejected until GitHub has the new one. The new value is never returned — call register-github-webhook next to update the hook on GitHub server-side, or copy the secret from the application's page in G8Deck.

| Parameter                                       | Type   | Description                                                       |
| ----------------------------------------------- | ------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `application` <span class="req">required</span> | string | Application uuid or slug.                                         |
| `organization`                                  | string | Organisation uuid or slug. Omit to use your default organisation. |

### `register-github-webhook`

<p class="tool-meta">Tier <code>mcp:write</code> · permission <code>deployments.update.item</code></p>

Create the push-to-deploy webhook on the application's GitHub repository, server-side, using the organisation's git credential for github.com — so the webhook secret never appears in this conversation. Switches push-to-deploy on (minting a secret if none exists). Idempotent: a hook already pointing at this application's URL is updated in place (events, content type and the current secret), which is also the step after rotate-deploy-webhook-secret. When the organisation's G8Deck GitHub App installation covers the repository, no hook is created — the App's app-level webhook already delivers its pushes — and the response says covered_by_github_app. Refused, with what to do, when the repository is not on github.com or no github.com credential with a token exists. GitHub then sends a ping, which get-deploy-webhook lists as an ignored delivery saying the webhook is wired correctly.

| Parameter                                       | Type   | Description                                                                                                         |
| ----------------------------------------------- | ------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `application` <span class="req">required</span> | string | Application uuid or slug.                                                                                           |
| `git_credential`                                | string | github.com git credential uuid to use. Default: the organisation's first active github.com credential with a token. |
| `organization`                                  | string | Organisation uuid or slug. Omit to use your default organisation.                                                   |

## Destructive tools

Each needs a token carrying `mcp:destroy`, and most also need an identifying value retyped into a confirmation argument. A mismatch is refused and audited.

### `destroy-deployment`

<p class="tool-meta">Tier <code>mcp:destroy</code> · permission <code>deployments.destroy.item</code></p>

Tear down a deployment and everything it provisioned. IRREVERSIBLE. Requires the deployment name retyped exactly in confirm_name, and a token carrying mcp:destroy. Both the destruction and any refused attempt are audited.

| Parameter                                        | Type   | Description                                                                 |
| ------------------------------------------------ | ------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `deployment` <span class="req">required</span>   | string | Deployment uuid or slug.                                                    |
| `confirm_name` <span class="req">required</span> | string | The deployment's exact name, retyped. Anything else is refused and audited. |
| `organization`                                   | string | Organisation uuid or slug. Omit to use your default organisation.           |

### `execute-rollback`

<p class="tool-meta">Tier <code>mcp:destroy</code> · permission <code>rollback.execute.rollback</code></p>

Roll a workload back to its previous release. Run plan-rollback first and check the target. Requires the workload name retyped in confirm_name and a token carrying mcp:destroy.

| Parameter                                        | Type   | Description                                                               |
| ------------------------------------------------ | ------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `workload` <span class="req">required</span>     | string | Attached workload uuid.                                                   |
| `confirm_name` <span class="req">required</span> | string | The workload's exact name, retyped. Anything else is refused and audited. |
| `organization`                                   | string | Organisation uuid or slug. Omit to use your default organisation.         |

### `delete-managed-cache`

<p class="tool-meta">Tier <code>mcp:destroy</code> · permission <code>managed-caches.delete.item</code> · organisation owner or administrator only</p>

Delete a managed cache instance. What happens depends on how it got here, and the response says which: an instance G8Deck INSTALLED is torn down — the daemon is stopped, its unit and config removed and its data directory deleted, and everything cached in it is gone for good. An ADOPTED instance is only un-recorded: the daemon keeps running, keeps its data and keeps billing on the machine it sits on. It is refused while any application is still attached, because a detach is a decision about that application's environment and belongs where an operator can see what stops working. Confirmation is the instance's ENDPOINT (host:port), not its name — names repeat across rows and retyping one confirms nothing. Requires a token carrying mcp:destroy.

| Parameter                                            | Type   | Description                                                                                                                          |
| ---------------------------------------------------- | ------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `managed_cache` <span class="req">required</span>    | string | Managed cache uuid, from list-managed-caches.                                                                                        |
| `confirm_endpoint` <span class="req">required</span> | string | The instance's exact endpoint as host:port, retyped — not its name, which repeats across rows. Anything else is refused and audited. |
| `organization`                                       | string | Organisation uuid or slug. Omit to use your default organisation.                                                                    |

### `delete-backup-destination`

<p class="tool-meta">Tier <code>mcp:destroy</code> · permission <code>backups.manage.destinations</code> · organisation owner or administrator only</p>

Delete a backup destination's RECORD. The bucket and every backup already stored in it are untouched and stay restorable, and the bucket keeps billing wherever it lives. Refused for G8Deck Storage, and refused while any backup policy (a deleted one included) still points at it — move them first with set-backup-policy-destination. Confirmation is the destination's `location` from list-backup-destinations, retyped. Requires a token carrying mcp:destroy.

| Parameter                                            | Type   | Description                                                                                                      |
| ---------------------------------------------------- | ------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `destination` <span class="req">required</span>      | string | Backup destination uuid, from list-backup-destinations.                                                          |
| `confirm_location` <span class="req">required</span> | string | The destination's exact `location` from list-backup-destinations, retyped. Anything else is refused and audited. |
| `organization`                                       | string | Organisation uuid or slug. Omit to use your default organisation.                                                |

### `remove-managed-service`

<p class="tool-meta">Tier <code>mcp:destroy</code> · permission <code>deployments.destroy.item</code></p>

Delete ONE managed service (a deployment-local database, cache …) from a live deployment, leaving the rest running. IRREVERSIBLE — its data goes. Refused while any application of the deployment still references it through an env token ({{ mysql.connection_string }}, {{ db.password }} …); the refusal names the application and key. `planned_outcome` says what happens: `purge` = a native shared daemon nothing else on the server uses is stopped, disabled, UNINSTALLED and its data directory deleted (if the daemon turns out to hold another database it falls back to `drop`); `drop` = another deployment or a managed database server shares the daemon, so only this deployment's database and account are dropped and the daemon keeps running; `teardown` = the provisioner's own teardown, as deleting the whole deployment would run it. Its vault connection string and cached tokens go too. Queued — poll get-deployment until the service is gone. A service that is already gone is a no-op. Requires the deployment SLUG retyped in confirm_slug and a token carrying mcp:destroy.

| Parameter                                           | Type   | Description                                                                                               |
| --------------------------------------------------- | ------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `deployment` <span class="req">required</span>      | string | Deployment uuid or slug.                                                                                  |
| `managed_service` <span class="req">required</span> | string | Managed service uuid, from get-deployment's managed_services.                                             |
| `confirm_slug` <span class="req">required</span>    | string | The deployment's exact SLUG, retyped (not its name — names repeat). Anything else is refused and audited. |
| `organization`                                      | string | Organisation uuid or slug. Omit to use your default organisation.                                         |
